summary: Frontend-only test of the Secret Layer LSB redesign, decoder, Autopsy D-06 country chart, content updates and full regressions, run in Chromium against the public preview URL. New suite /app/tests/portfolio_secret_layer.py: 13/13 passed. Updated portfolio_runtime.py: 19/19 passed. Updated portfolio_edges.py: 7/7 passed. Canvas pixels match the PNG LSB planes exactly (mean diff <0.002). Plate 01 blue, Plate 02 red and Plate 03 green show the letters at plane 0. Every other channel at plane 0 is noise (centre ~0.50 vs ~0.65-0.73). Planes 1-7 are identical across channels, so brightness or levels cannot reveal anything. Offline numpy check of the plates: OU, TL and OUD found. SHA-256 hash = sha256('outloud'). No application bugs found.

issues: The answer is the site brand: 'Out Loud' appears in the nav logo, hero ('/ Out Loud'), footer, <title>, meta description and build-log entry 02 ('Condensed the Out Loud concept...'). The secret section DOM never contains the answer, and the uppercase 'OUT LOUD' never appears before solving. Even so, a visitor can guess the phrase without decoding. This needs a product decision, not a code bug.
Number format is inconsistent: South Korea shows '1.5k' while the others show 2 decimals ('1.71k'). The replace(/0$/) trims only one zero, so a value such as 2000 would render '2.0k'.

action_items: Optional: decide whether the visible 'Out Loud' brand name is an acceptable giveaway for the puzzle answer.
Optional: make the chart number format consistent (e.g. always 2 decimals, or trim trailing zeros fully).
critical_code_review_comments: SecretLayer reset() clears spoiler but keeps hintLevel, channel and plane. After reset, the bench still shows the correct channel at plane 0 with all hints visible. Minor; decide whether reset should fully restore the start state.
The hint button uses aria-disabled at level 3 but stays clickable (it is a no-op via Math.min). Harmless.
Plate tab thumbnails load the full ~0.7-1.1 MB PNGs (plus a 1.7 MB master plate in the decoder). Acceptable, but heavy on mobile.
The decoder takes channels R, G and B LSBs sequentially, while the comment says 'red pixel' only. The comment is stale.
